prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S164: Lantern issues a crew exposure refresh only after the current reconnaissance confidence and weather timing fields are both valid.
S165: Hazards shown to crews include unstable snags, limited access, steep slope exposure, utility conflicts, and escape route degradation.
S166: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides weather-derived exposure flags that support staging decisions near ridgelines and drainages.
S167: When the system enters the Airspace Restricted State, helitack assignments show the restriction boundary and require confirmation before aircraft-dependent movement is planned.
S168: The Drone Tasking Service maintains reconnaissance task status so that ground teams can see whether requested intelligence is pending, active, or complete.
S169: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock status is shown as an availability input only and does not by itself authorize crew movement into a new area.
S170: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms launch readiness separately from crew assignment acceptance to keep reconnaissance execution independent from ground deployment.
S171: The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater mirrors priority assignment summaries for crews that cannot maintain a data session in canyon or timbered terrain.
S172: If the data link is degraded, the Crewline Mobile Tablet presents the last verified assignment package and clearly identifies the time of last update.
S173: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges assignment receipt, reports readiness, and records any exception that prevents safe execution.
S174: The County Emergency Liaison can view staging posture and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter crew assignments or hazard records.
S175: All assignment and staging changes preserve an audit trail so that later reviews can reconstruct what information was available to each crew at the time of action.
S176: During prolonged wildfire operations, the system shall favor continuity of command decisions over full automation when communications, power, or sensor coverage is impaired.
S177: The Caldera Incident Command Portal enters a disconnected operating mode when its primary network path is unavailable and clearly marks all displayed information with the last synchronization time.
S178: In disconnected operating mode, the Caldera Incident Command Portal allows authorized users to review cached incident data and create queued updates, but it prevents irreversible releases until connectivity is restored.
S179: The Duty Detection Officer receives a visible warning whenever a detection, assignment, or hazard record is based on stale data or partial sensor coverage.
S180: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine shall continue using the last approved model configuration after a repository outage and shall reject unversioned rules or unsigned analytic packages.
